`, now terminates the paragraph and emits a stray empty `

`. union.summary: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws at module-import time, so a markdown-it upgrade takes down the whole notes preview rather than degrading one rendering case

union.summary: `Ruler.at('lheading', ...)` is called without an `options.alt`, discarding whatever alt chain the installed markdown-it registers for `lheading`
union.evidence: `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule);` at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175 passes no options, while the very next `at()` call (:197-199) does pass `{ alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] }` precisely because, as the change's own lessons file records, `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` REPLACES the rule's \`alt\` chain with \`options.alt || []\` (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:19). The author applied that lesson to `list` and not to `lheading`. In markdown-it 14.x's `parser_block` registry `lheading` is declared with no alt chain, so this is likely harmless today — but it is an unguarded assumption about a third-party private table, and if the pinned version (or a future bump) gives `lheading` any alt membership, it silently stops terminating paragraphs/blockquotes/references for consumers well outside this file. To confirm, check `node_modules/markdown-it/lib/parser_block.mjs` for the `lheading` entry's third element. Fix belongs on the new code: pass the upstream alt chain back explicitly, as was done for `list`.

union.summary: Plugin ordering: `listEmptyBulletPlugin` runs after `detailsPlugin` and re-registers `list`/`lheading`, clobbering any alt chain or wrapper those earlier plugins installed on the same rules
union.evidence: `preview.ts` applies plugins in sequence — `md.use(detailsPlugin)` (preview.ts:43) then `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` (preview.ts:47) — and the new plugin calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:175) and `md.block.ruler.at('list', ...)` (:197) which overwrite both the fn and the alt chain of those rules. `getRuleFn(md, 'list')` (:179) captures whatever fn is installed at that moment, so a `list` wrapper from `detailsPlugin` survives, but `lheading` is replaced outright with no delegation and the restored `alt` for `list` is hardcoded to markdown-it's stock `['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` — dropping any alt membership (e.g. a `details` context) an earlier plugin added. `details-plugin.ts` is not in the diff and is not present in this checkout, so I could not verify whether it touches `list`/`lheading`; the new file's header comment references it (`same note as in \`details-plugin.ts\``), confirming it exists. To confirm, open `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts` and grep it for `block.ruler`, `ruler.at`, `ruler.before`, and `alt:`.

union.summary: A throw from `getRuleFn` at module scope takes down the entire `@wafflebase/notes` public entry point, not just the preview — including the store and toolbar surfaces that never touch markdown.
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:212) throws `markdown-it block rule not found: list` if markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry shape changes. It is invoked from `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at preview.ts:48, which is *module top-level*. The out-of-diff blast radius is the import chain: packages/notes/src/index.ts:12 re-exports `initialize` from `./view/editor.js`, and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20 statically imports `NotePreview` from `./preview.js`. So evaluating the package barrel evaluates preview.ts. Every frontend consumer therefore fails to import, not just the preview pane: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:7, notes-detail.tsx:9, notes-toolbar.tsx:7, and yorkie-note-store.ts:7 (the Yorkie CRDT note store, which has nothing to do with markdown rendering). `packages/notes/package.json:63` pins `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"` (caret) and harness.config.json:45 enables `dependencyFreshness` with `failOnCritical`, so an automated bump is a live path. Fix belongs on the new code: make `getRuleFn` degrade (return a no-op / skip the wrap) instead of throwing during module evaluation, or move the `md.use` behind a lazily-initialised renderer.

union.summary: The CodeMirror source pane still parses these lines as setext headings, so in split view the editor and the preview now disagree about the same text.

For input like `foo\n -` (4-space indent, not inside a list) `wrappedList` returns `true` in silent mode, ending the paragraph; the `code` rule then claims the line, changing `foo
-` into a paragraph plus an indented code block containing `-`. This is outside the documented scope of the deviation (docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299) and no added test covers it. Flagging as reachable-behaviour scope creep; the correctness lens may also own the condition itself.
